subject: ClockOracle R6 PowerShell runner
scope: Independent source-only runner review and partial numeric census. No source execution, parsing of authored code, imports, compilation, tests, CI, app or device activity.

convention.scalar: Count reached scalar/literal reads; actual destination initialization/writes; arithmetic/bitwise/comparison/boolean/conversion; selected branches; dispatch/entry/return; and every actual loop/control event once. All own helpers, callers, defaults, reference formation, receiver/property/access and administration remain expanded.
convention.leaf: Count evaluated caller arguments/reference formation and dispatch, plus the declared primitive boundary's entry and return. An actually reached visible wrapper has its own entry/body/return. Existing CLR/JSON/OS/CRT/libm/intrinsic internal CPU remains opaque; selected C++ SDK and all own helpers are expanded.
convention.transfers: External scalar/result/out-buffer destination writes occur once. Guaranteed result initialization into the caller destination is not another transfer. Caller evaluation supplies a by-value source read, parameter initialization supplies its write without a second source read. Reference binding copies no referent cells.
convention.payload: Opaque primitive CPU and general heap/RSS exclusions do not remove controlled arrays, configured stream buffers, clones, capacities, preprocessing, retained owners, or lifetime obligations. Null/local exit is not physical GC reclamation.
convention.notProductionModel: Production ADR0085 O/A/F logical primitive prices and branch/literal convention are not imported.
convention.bulk: Existing declared bulk CRT/CLR primitive effects are represented by the counted call boundary and visible caller arguments/wrappers: do not add n internal byte destination writes or one invented bulk-scalar write. Scalar results/out-parameters have one actual destination write. All byte extents and controlled payload/lifetime obligations remain. Actual visible aggregate element initialization/copy expands; opaque CLR internals do not.
